why:
It is the only candidate whose load-bearing claims I could reproduce, and the only one that caught the two things that would have silently sunk this run.

(1) The ledger defect. The prior-art ledger rules "reuse propertyCarrying, no new capability" and cites `arch.yaml:211`. I read it: line 211's `role: name` sits on the **`word`** entity's `name` property ("The name it is shown by"). `member.name` is at `arch.yaml:519-521`, written `is: name` with **no role**. So `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, 'member', ROLES.name)` returns `undefined` today, and an IMPLEMENT worker reading the ledger literally ships a `data-member` that never appears and an intended target that cannot match. `most-general` reaches the same route but by assertion, and neither it nor `simplest` catches that the ledger's own evidence is pointed at the wrong property.

(2) The verification-harness trap. I reproduced the measurement on bun 1.2.14 in this worktree: `HTMLRewriter.getAttribute('data-declaration')` returns `"a"b&c<d>e'f"`, which is **not** equal to the raw id; a plain descendant selector matches 1; an escaped-value selector matches **0** where a browser matches 1. So the no-dependency harness silently disagrees with the browser on exactly the "punctuation and quotes in an id" case issue #114 requires — it passes wrongly, or gets "fixed" by softening the fixture. Neither other candidate noticed the harness at all.

It also wins on the member-identity route on verified evidence the others missed. The test-only `equivalent` entity (`app.test.tsx:1074-1078`) declares `properties: { language: { is: 'string' }, name: { is: 'string' } }`. Its first column is `language`, so "first column" breaks on a shape already in this repo's tests — and its `name` column is typed **`string`**, not `name`, so `simplest`'s "the property whose declared type is MetaLang's `name`" finds **nothing** on it. `simplest`'s route is not more general than the role route; it is less general, and it is two answers to a question `words.ts:395-404` documents itself as solely owning ("This is the one place the question 'which property of this type carries that role' is answered") — SOLID rail 1 and rail 4, plus SOLID rail 3 for baking a type's spelling into the renderer.

Its rules are the only set that bites on measured facts: `app.tsx` holds **zero** `'name'`/`"name"` literals today (grep count 0), so R1 lands with no carve-out; the render path holds **zero** clock/random/env uses (the only two hits in all of `ts/metalang` are `bundle.ts:148` bundler-define and `examples.ts:140` `process.cwd` for a hand-written page), so R3 locks a property that is true now and guarded by nothing; and no byte-identity test exists anywhere in `ts/metalang` (`examples.test.ts:119-120` is a re-colour idempotence check, a different thing), so R4 locks a property GROUND proved by probe and nothing holds.

And it found a live release defect the others did not: `ci.yml:591` checks `kit.js page.js package.json README.md metalang.yaml arch.yaml propose.yaml`, while `kit.ts:74-75` carries `style.css` and `syntax.css` and the job's own comment says "the three languages and the two stylesheets." This work forces a kit release straight into that gap.

Where it is wrong, I measured it and corrected it rather than adopting it: see the placement graft below.
synthesizedApproach:
ADOPT risk-first, with the helper-tag placement grafted from simplest/most-general and the resolver kept test-scope.

== THREE DECISIONS GATE IMPLEMENT (none is defaultable; leaving any to the implementer is a rails-decisions "undecided forced choice") ==

D1 — how a member row finds its identity. My pick: add `role: name` to `member.name` in `ts/metalang/arch.yaml` (line ~519), and widen the `role: name` doc text in `ts/metalang/metalang.yaml:1011-1018` from the display-scoped wording ("It holds the name this thing is shown by… drawn with that name beside the id where the two differ") to "the name this thing is known by", so the renderer asks the ONE existing owner `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` (`words.ts:422`). The other two routes are engineering-eliminated, not preferences — see autoResolved #1. Cost: a change to a language file carried in the kit, which `selector-contract.md` says "changes the language and needs its own approval". I verified it is drawing-safe: all three `ROLES.name` consumers (`app.tsx:577` shownBy, `app.tsx:683` Rungs, `propose.ts:405`) reach the type only through `typeOfOwnValue` of a closed set, and `member` appears exactly once in the languages, as `list: { of: member }` (`arch.yaml:582`), never as an enum's own-value type — so no existing page changes. `distinct: { in: properties, by: role }` (`metalang.yaml:1163`) stays satisfied: member would carry kind, prose, name. No test blocks it — `words.test.ts:548-552` asserts `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, 'member', ROLES.kind)` only, and says nothing about name.

D2 — what the acceptance resolves selectors with. My pick: one pinned DOM devDependency (happy-dom), because I reproduced that bun's built-in HTMLRewriter cannot do this honestly (see `why`). A dependency is explicitly Tim's under rails-decisions. The no-dependency alternative is to prove escaping by DECODING the attribute and prove uniqueness only on plain ids, and to state plainly that browser-equivalent matching of a quoted id is NOT proven in-repo — that is an honest weaker proof, never a silent swap.

D3 — where the helper tag sits. My pick, and the graft that corrects risk-first: **after the `#page-data` script and before the bundle script, so the bundle stays last.** risk-first put it last, before `</html>`. I ran the existing slice logic and it breaks: with the helper last, `html.lastIndexOf('</script>')` lands on the HELPER's closing tag, so the slice becomes `var a = "<\/script>"</script>\n<script src="/api/packages/story.js">`, which contains `</script` and FAILS the two existing escaping assertions at `render.test.ts:96` and `render.test.ts:146`. Before-the-bundle keeps both passing (measured: slice = `var a = "<\/script>"`), keeps `#page-data` ahead of the bundle (`client.tsx:15-16` throws otherwise), and the tag carries an attribute so `indexOf('<script>')` still skips it. risk-first's stated reason for last — "gives the helper a mounted DOM" — is also wrong: `createRoot(root).render()` schedules, so NO position in this shell guarantees a mounted DOM. Its other reason (an earlier classic script blocks the parse until a 404 resolves outside JARVIS) is real but costs a delay, not the page. The decisive fact is that `story.js` belongs to JARVIS and is unreadable from this repository, so its load-order expectation cannot be proven here — the JARVIS lane (4thWAIV/jarvis#120) confirms, and until it does this is an open item, not an auto-resolution.

== THE BUILD ==

1. Shell. `pageHtml` (`render.ts:60-72`) emits the settled tag verbatim — `<script src="/api/packages/story.js"></script>` — from one exported named constant, no interpolation, on its own line after the data block and before the bundle. Pin the whole shell with a byte-exact assertion, not `toContain`, so the position is locked rather than remembered. Both the repo `render` command and the kit go through `pageHtml`, so one change reaches both after a kit rebuild.

2. Declaration identity. In `Declaration` (`app.tsx:1468`), the `section.d-decl` takes `data-declaration={body.id}` under the SAME predicate already written at `app.tsx:1480` and `app.tsx:1500` (`typeof body.id === 'string' && body.id.length > 0`), extracted to one named const consumed by the `d-id` span, the `Err`, and the new attribute, so the three cannot drift (DRY rail 5 — graft from most-general, sharpened by risk-first). No id → no attribute; the existing `no id` em and the `Err` at `app.tsx:1500-1502` already report it. The value goes through JSX, so React escapes it. No existing test asserts the section's opening tag (verified: the only `d-decl` assertions, `app.test.tsx:201` and `:206`, are on the `d-decl-head` div), so this is byte-safe.

3. Member identity. `Table` (`app.tsx:718-785`) asks `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` ONCE per table, beside `columns`. Each data `<tr>` takes `data-member={text(member[part])}` when that yields a non-empty string. The `tr.r-note` sibling (`app.tsx:773-779`) never does, and the existing mark `className`/`id` are untouched. No property is named by spelling, so a shape whose identifying column is called anything, in any position, works. Verified safe: there are no `<tr` substring assertions anywhere in the test files, and the existing `data-col` assertions (`app.test.tsx:1098-1110`, `:1544`) are on `th`/`td`, not the row.

4. Zero and two carriers, loudness reused not reinvented. Zero carriers → the row carries no attribute and no error, which is the owner's own documented contract (`words.ts:425-428`: "A thing whose type answers none of the three draws as it drew before the language had the word"); the loud half is the resolver reporting the target as missing. Two carriers → `propertyCarrying` returns undefined, so again no attribute, and NOTHING NEW is written: the page's existing `Err` at `app.tsx:1087-1093` already names both carriers, and the checker already faults it through `distinct: { in: properties, by: role }`.

5. One target-resolution owner, test-scope. A single helper every selector assertion goes through: `resolve(html, selector)` → exactly-one / missing(selector) / ambiguous(count). It never substitutes a broader selector and never takes the first of several; missing and ambiguous both fail loudly naming the selector and the count. It stays test-scope — no `ts/metalang/target.ts` shipped in the renderer and no `kit.js target` command (the cut from most-general; see autoResolved #8).

6. Acceptance, RED first, all in the existing test files. (a) The real in-repo document `ts/metalang/parts.yaml` — eight declarations, four member lists with rows plus two `members: none` — every declaration id resolves to exactly one section, every `[data-declaration="X"] [data-part="members"]` to exactly one, every member row by name inside its own declaration. (b) An inline fixture declaring its OWN entity with `role: name` against a language that is not `arch`, proving the mechanism is language-agnostic and not an arch special case (real-work rail 3). (c) A member name repeated across two declarations — `parts.yaml`'s names are distinct, so this needs the inline fixture; each target resolves to exactly one. (d) An id carrying `"`, `'`, `&`, `<`, `>`: assert the DECODED attribute value equals the id exactly, and that the escaped selector resolves to one — never a substring assertion. (e) Duplicate declaration ids → the resolver reports ambiguous (`app.test.tsx:100` proves duplicates are possible). (f) A shape with no name role → no `data-member`, resolver reports missing. (g) Every existing `data-part`/`data-col` assertion passes untouched. (h) Byte identity, which does not exist today: one document rendered twice compared byte for byte, and two kit builds compared per file. (i) Through the built kit: `node kit.js render` output carries the helper tag, reusing the `kit.test.ts:193-207` pattern on `parts.yaml`, and the built `page.js` executed in the DOM yields the same resolved targets as the component render — the only proof that what JARVIS downloads carries the change.

7. Release. The change moves `page.js` and `kit.js` and therefore the digest, so a new kit release through the existing `ci.yml` release job is the delivery. Rule 9 below must land FIRST: `ci.yml:591` omits `style.css` and `syntax.css` from the required-file check while `kit.ts:74-75` carries them. Then hand Diagnostics the four facts `selector-contract.md` names — tag, forty-character sha, SHA-256 of `evolang-kit.zip`, download URL — and re-cut revision `33c6c6b3…` of `document-40f2beb547b345b9b35d75d728e538c1` before any beat is written against the new targets. Already-signed packages stay immutable.

8. Rule mechanism. Contract-directed test rules that scan source and run inside the `bun test` step CI already executes, each with a violating fixture proving it fires and a compliant one proving it does not. `eslint.config.js` wires only `@eslint/js` and `typescript-eslint` with no local plugin (verified), and adding a plugin mechanism is a design element that outlives its function. In-repo precedent: `examples.test.ts` walks the repository root; on the .NET side `EvidenceUploadsCannotRegressTests.cs` reads `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

risks: The prior-art ledger's reuse verdict is pointed at the wrong property and must not be carried into IMPLEMENT as written. It rules 'reuse propertyCarrying, no new capability' citing arch.yaml:211 — but that role: name sits on the `word` entity ('The name it is shown by'), while member.name at arch.yaml:519-521 is `is: name` with no role. propertyCarrying(bodyOf, 'member', ROLES.name) returns undefined today. Taken at face value, IMPLEMENT ships a data-member that never appears and [data-member="BeginVerification"] cannot match. This is why D1 is a decision and not a reuse.

Bun's built-in HTMLRewriter cannot be trusted for this acceptance. Reproduced on bun 1.2.14 in this worktree: getAttribute returns raw entity text (a"b&c<d>e'f, not equal to the id) and a selector carrying an escaped value matched 0 elements, while a plain descendant selector matched 1 and a browser matches both. Verification built on it silently passes the quoted-id case issue #114 requires. D2 exists for this; the no-dependency fallback proves escaping only by decoding and must state plainly that browser-equivalent matching of a quoted id is not proven in-repo.

Helper-tag placement cannot be settled from this repository and must not be auto-resolved. story.js belongs to JARVIS and is unreadable here, so its load-order expectation is unproven. Two measured facts bound the choice: placing it LAST breaks the existing escaping assertions at render.test.ts:96 and :146 (lastIndexOf('</script>') then lands on the helper's closing tag), and createRoot().render() schedules, so no position in this shell guarantees the helper a mounted DOM. Default is after the data block and before the bundle; the JARVIS lane (4thWAIV/jarvis#120) confirms before a beat is written.

D1 changes a language file carried in the kit and widens the recorded meaning of role: name from the display-scoped wording at metalang.yaml:1011-1018 to row identity. Tim must approve both the arch.yaml line and the doc rewording; the contract may not record either as decided until he says yes. Verified drawing-safe (all three ROLES.name consumers reach the type via typeOfOwnValue of a closed set; member is used only as `list: { of: member }` at arch.yaml:582; distinct-by-role stays satisfied; no test asserts member has no name role), but safe is not approved.

The rendered page's #root is empty — the DOM is drawn in the browser by page.js. A selector test aimed at the CLI output finds zero matches, and the obvious 'fix' is to loosen the assertion. Every target assertion must run against the Page component render (the same root client.tsx mounts) or against the executed bundle.

Shapes whose language declares no role: name property get rows with no data-member, and the silence is closed only at target-resolution time by the resolver reporting 'missing'. If Tim wants it caught at render time instead — an on-page Err band or a render failure — that is a different and larger cost: it would change how pages that draw such shapes render today, including the test-only `equivalent` entity.

Duplicate declaration ids are legitimate: app.test.tsx:100 pins 'one id declared twice keeps the first', so [data-declaration="X"] can match two cards and the page draws both. The issue names only the repeated-member-name case; the duplicate-id case is the one that would silently ring the wrong card, so the acceptance must cover it and the resolver must report ambiguous rather than take the first. Whether to refuse duplicates at check time is a separate open question.

The two literal targets cannot be proven in this repository. No MetaLang document here declares IGrantStore or IWindowsHelloNativeOps, and the nine-declaration surface lives in the JARVIS document store (document-40f2beb547b345b9b35d75d728e538c1). In-repo acceptance proves the general property on parts.yaml plus fixtures; the two literal targets are verified on the JARVIS side after the kit release. Writing those two ids into a repo fixture is the hardcoded-specific cheat rule 2 bans.

The kit release is blocked on the ci.yml gap until rule 10 lands: ci.yml:591 omits style.css and syntax.css from the required-file check while kit.ts:74-75 carries them. A kit released from this branch before that fix could be refused by JARVIS at adoption, and the failure would surface only there.

The language change means every document checked under the old kit needs revalidating and a new revision; revision 33c6c6b3… of document-40f2beb547b345b9b35d75d728e538c1 must be re-cut before any beat is written against the new targets, and already-signed packages stay immutable. The kit digest moves once, and JARVIS stage/activate needs its compatibility review — outside this repository's control.

Byte determinism was probed only under bun 1.2.14 on one machine, and the zip stores mtimes, so the released asset's SHA-256 is not reproducible even when the kit's contents are. The byte-identity gate covers per-file contents, not the zip.

Executing the built page.js in a DOM may be slow or flaky. If that leg is dropped, the proof of the BUILT bundle degrades to a string check on page.js — a weaker claim that must be reported as such, never quietly swapped in.
The ts coverage floor is 0.75 (bunfig.toml, matching eng/coverage-gate.sh). New renderer code carries its own tests or the gate fails; lowering the floor or dropping a leg to get green is out.
